title: Atomic token commit and client backpressure signalization to eliminate partial response flicker
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
On 2026-02-27 we observed a P0 incident where hosted streaming responses intermittently delivered truncated or partial tokens to clients during transient capacity spikes and scheduler preemption. Clients saw short bursts of token "flicker" (e.g., half-tokens, duplicated fragments) followed by either reconnection or silent truncation. This degraded UX for low-latency streaming workloads and caused multiple customers to file support tickets.

What happened (short):
- During a capacity spike, the serving runtime preempted in-progress streams to reassign GPU work.
- The streaming flush path allowed partial token fragments to be propagated to the socket buffer before the runtime completed token-assembly and KV-cache reconciliation.
- Under backpressure conditions, we observed race windows where a connection would be signaled closed / throttled while the token buffer had not yet committed atomically, resulting in client-visible partial tokens or duplicate replays after reconnect.

Root cause (summary):
1) Non-atomic flush of token assembly across the runtime pipeline: intermediate byte-fragments could be emitted if a write was interrupted.
2) Backpressure and connection lifecycle signals are currently coarse-grained: the scheduler would preempt a worker without a per-connection graceful drain requiring a synchronous commit or abort.
3) KV-cache eviction and async refresh occasionally caused the token assembly to be delayed; when combined with preemption the commit race widened.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: partial tokens / flicker, reconnect retries, and occasional semantic corruption of streamed responses.
- Scope: multi-tenant hosted pools on the v2 runtime under high burst load; affected ~7% of streaming sessions during the incident window.
- Business: elevated support, temporary mitigation via increased retry timeouts for top customers.

Investigation timeline (high level):
- 2026-02-27 10:22 UTC: Monitoring alerted on increased streaming error and dropped-token rates.
- 2026-02-27 11:05 UTC: Initial mitigation: throttled burst path and increased session drain timeout.
- 2026-02-28 to 2026-03-01: Reproduction harness built; identified race between write-flush and preemption.
- 2026-03-02: Design proposal created and reviewed with runtime and infra.

Design proposal (what we will build):
Goal: eliminate client-visible partial tokens by making token emissions atomic and providing explicit per-connection backpressure/soft-drain signals so the scheduler can coordinate preemption without producing partial output.

High-level changes:
- Atomic token commit at runtime edge: buffer token assembly in an in-memory atomic buffer per connection, only flush to socket after commit is complete. This buffer is isolated from KV-cache refresh paths and uses a single writer/committer model.
- Connection soft-drain and preemption handshake: add a lightweight RPC between scheduler and worker that requests "soft-drain" on a connection, giving up to X ms (configurable) to commit or abort pending tokens before preemption. Default X=150 ms (tunable).
- Explicit backpressure signalization: surface per-connection state and queue depth via metrics and a new event stream to the control plane so autoscaler/scheduler can make informed preemption decisions.
- Client SDK/HTTP contract improvements: add idempotency/resume token at stream start and document resume semantics so clients can de-duplicate replays safely.

Action items (concrete):
1) Runtime change: implement per-connection atomic token buffer and commit API (owner: runtime-team -- Rajat). Estimate: 3 points.
2) Scheduler change: implement soft-drain handshake and respect drain timeout; add config knobs to tune preemption behavior (owner: infra-scheduler -- Priya Kapoor). Estimate: 2 points.
3) KV-cache hardening: ensure async refresh doesn't extend commit window; add opportunistic refresh and priority for in-flight streams (owner: serving-cache -- Luca Chen). Estimate: 2 points.
4) SDK updates: add resume-id header and docs; implement client-side retry that prefers resume over full re-request (owner: dx-sdk -- Maria Gomez). Estimate: 1 point.
5) Observability: add metrics (partial_token_emits, soft_drain_latency, commit_time_ms, in_flight_token_bytes) and dashboards; create alert when partial_token_emits > 0.01% of streams (owner: observability -- Jordan Lee). Estimate: 1 point.
6) E2E test harness: synthetic chaos tests that simulate preemption and KV-cache delays; add to CI gating for streaming critical path (owner: qa -- Tom Baker). Estimate: 2 points.

Progress updates and decisions:
- 2026-03-03: Spike completed for atomic buffer. Prototype shows zero partial emits under simulated preemption. Decision: adopt single-writer buffer per connection rather than lock-free multi-writer to reduce complexity (trade-off: slightly higher latency under high concurrency but far safer).
- 2026-03-05: Scheduler soft-drain handshake design reviewed with infra. Agreed default drain timeout 150 ms; allow override via pool config.
- 2026-03-07: Security review: no customer data leaves process boundaries; KMS/HSM unaffected. Security review not required for this change (logged).
- 2026-03-09: Observability metric names and alert thresholds locked in; dashboard PR prepared: https://grafana.redwood.io/d/streaming/partial-token-dashboard.
- 2026-03-11: Runtime PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5482 (WIP).

Acceptance criteria (how we know it's fixed):
- Unit and integration tests for atomic commit pass in CI.
- Canary on 5% of production traffic for 24 hours shows partial_token_emits <= 0.001% and no increase in end-to-end latency > 5th percentile baseline.
- Support tickets referencing "partial token" or "flicker" drop to baseline for 14 days after full rollout.
- Release: enable as opt-in feature flag on runtime-1.20, then full rollout in runtime-1.20.1.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1: Merge runtime atomic commit behind feature flag; enable in internal staging; run synthetic chaos for 48h. (Owners: Rajat, Tom)
- Phase 2: Canary 5% production with telemetry; monitor metrics and error budgets for 24h. (Owners: Rajat, Jordan)
- Phase 3: Increase canary to 25% for 24h; if stable, roll to 100%. Implement dynamic revert if partial_token_emits spike.

Monitoring & alerting:
- New alert: streaming.partial_token_emits.rate > 0.01% for 10m -> P0 paging.
- Dashboard: partial-token breakdown by pool, model, and route.
- Post-rollout check: run synthetic replay test every 6 hours for the first 72 hours.

Open trade-offs and follow-ups:
- We chose single-writer atomic buffer to reduce correctness risk; long-term we can explore lock-free batching for throughput gains.
- Tune drain-timeout: 150 ms is conservative; may tune lower if latency impact observed.
- Explore coalescing resume tokens with KV-cache snapshots so resume is faster and less likely to cause semantic duplication.
